## Source transition and recovery contract

The control core reserves `intent.json` with exclusive creation in a canonical,
owner0700 journal, owner0600 append-only files and file/directory fsync, before calling a
performer. The exact selected journal root/operation path prevents changing the
local output path to replay that selection. Existing intent means no second
dispatch. A future executor must independently verify and protect the authored
control/selection/journal-root binding before Python startup and hold the
actual exclusive target lease; these source checks are not a hostile same-UID
or global atomicity guarantee. Directory-fsync failure refuses before a performer
call; actual crash/power-loss durability on the target remains unqualified.

Forward requires the complete known prior map; ordinary recovery requires the
complete known forward map. An explicitly reviewed **owned partial** recovery
must bind the original private forward journal path, intent and held outcome byte hashes,
the separately reviewed exact current full map, matching source/site/root and
a new operation. Every surviving partial path must have known prior/forward
bytes and mode. The full actual target map must equal that reviewed partial map.
This does not discover, approve or recover an unknown partial state automatically.
A copy failure alone authorizes no recovery. The real admission performer must
also establish no FIELD start/journals/native state requiring the newer runtime.

`capture()` persists raw command stdout/stderr/return or caught exception
class/message/trace/partial streams before asserting expected outcomes. A
nonzero copy, missing required effect, cache failure, malformed response,
poststate drift, lost result or interrupted intent is held/UNKNOWN with no retry
or reverse copy. Oversized records or storage errors cannot qualify completion;
the existing durable intent remains unresolved. The five existing required
effects remain activation-of-already-active, active readback, object-cache flush,
Kinsta page-cache purge and final version readback. Actual native effect and
continuity verification is a separate mandatory performer method; a list of
effect names alone cannot complete the transition. Final full byte/mode equality
is mandatory. Installed/served/FPM/human/device evidence remains separate.

A completed repeat validates the exact original plan/intent/completion and
fresh source/prior/target/continuity observations. It runs no copy or effect
commands and writes no journal file. Held or drifted state never becomes repeat
PASS. Observe/admission/verification collaborators must themselves be read-only
and preserve actual continuity; that capability is currently unsupported live.
